other_material_facts.label: industry_evidence
other_material_facts.value: Indian Media & Entertainment Industry Estimated Market Size of Media & Entertainment Industry Indian media and entertainment (M&E) sector demonstrated substantial growth, with an annual increase of INR80 billion.

other_material_facts.label: industry_evidence
other_material_facts.value: Between CY 2019 and CY 2025, the sector has expanded at a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of approximately 5.7%, rising from INR 1.92 trillion to a projected INR 2.68 trillion, surpassing pre-pandemic levels.

other_material_facts.label: industry_evidence
other_material_facts.value: Increased production, coupled with box office successes and evolving audience preferences, have propelled the industry's market size to a substantial INR 187 billion in 2024 from INR 72 billion in 2020.

other_material_facts.label: industry_evidence
other_material_facts.value: This impressive growth trajectory, reflecting a CAGR of approximately 27%, underscores the industry's robust health and its potential for continued expansion.

other_material_facts.label: industry_evidence
other_material_facts.value: The Indian M&E sector is expected to grow at a 7% CAGR, reaching INR 3.06 trillion (USD 37.1 billion) by 2027 from INR 2.50 trillion in 2024.

other_material_facts.label: industry_evidence
other_material_facts.value: Digital media is expected to grow at a CAGR of 11.2%, significantly showing a better growth rate compared to other segments.

other_material_facts.label: industry_evidence
other_material_facts.value: Localization and regional content are emerging as crucial growth drivers.

other_material_facts.label: industry_evidence
other_material_facts.value: Expected growth in film entertainment segment and Insights on emerging growth pattern The film entertainment segment is expected to grow at a CAGR of 4.4%, reaching INR 213 billion by 2027, up from INR 187 billion in 2024.

other_material_facts.label: industry_evidence
other_material_facts.value: Emerging Growth Patterns • Expansion into Tier II and III Markets: Tier II and III cities are emerging as significant growth drivers for the film industry.

other_material_facts.label: industry_evidence
other_material_facts.value: Individual growth of the Indian AVOD segment is anticipated to reach US$ 2.6 billion by FY25 end rising at a CAGR of 24%, while the Indian entertainment sector could unlock an estimated Rs. 50,724 crore (US$ 6 billion) in unrealised value by FY30. 2Driven by the push from platforms like Samsung TV+ and JioTV+, which can be viewed on Connected TV sets, surge in smartphone ownerships, improved broadband infrastructure and huge demand for regional content that caters to the country’s linguistic diversity in India, this tiered segment of M&E industry is set to see a massive growth.

other_material_facts.label: industry_evidence
other_material_facts.value: These key drivers have significantly contributed to the revenue generation of the OTT businesses, making them grow at a remarkable CAGR of 14.9%, the highest among the top 15 countries, to reach Rs. 35,061 crore (US$ 4.25 billion) by FY28. 5 Growth in OTT sector in India Mapping historical trend in growth The OTT sector in India has witnessed explosive growth, fuelled by improved internet access, affordability, and shifting consumer preferences.

other_material_facts.label: industry_evidence
other_material_facts.value: The rural sector is expected to grow at a 6% compound annual growth rate (CAGR), compared to 2.5% in urban areas.

other_material_facts.label: working_capital
other_material_facts.value: Year-Wise Detailed Rationale for Increase in Working Capital Requirements (Past 3FY) The increase in WCR is attributable to several factors inherent to the content production industry: (a) Expansion of Projects & Scale: Larger slate of films, web series, and digital projects requiring upfront investment. (b) Receivable Cycles: Broadcasters/OTTs operate on 75–90 day cycles, occasionally longer. (c) High Pre-Production & Talent Costs: Substantial costs precede invoicing. (d) IPO Proceeds: Reduce reliance on trade payables, allowing quicker settlements.

other_material_facts.label: debt_repayment
other_material_facts.value: Conclusion for RHP The Company’s working capital requirements are driven by its project-based model, with upfront investments in content creation recovered after delivery and approval cycles by major OTT/broadcast clients. • Debtors: Justified at ~85 days due to milestone-based billing and industry payment cycles. • Trade Payables: Maintained at low levels (40–35 days) consistent with service-oriented cost structure and liquidity from IPO proceeds. • Inventory: High due to ongoing and unreleased projects, consistent with production cycles.

risks.body:
- The loss of, or a significant reduction in orders from, any of our major customers could have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition, results of operations and prospects.
- A significant portion of our revenue is derived from a limited number of customers, primarily major television broadcasters, film studios and Over-the-Top (OTT) platforms.

- We cannot assure you that we will be able to maintain our relationships with our existing customers or that we will be able to secure new customers to replace any lost revenue.
- Any significant delay in the production process can lead to cost overruns, which may not be recoverable from our clients.
- We derive a majority of our revenues from a limited number of customers, including broadcasters, film studios, OTT platforms and distributors.
- For the Fiscal 2026, our top five customers accounted for approximately 85.05% of our revenue.
- For Fiscal 2025 and Fiscal 2024, the top five customers contributed 78.91% and 99.93% of revenues respectively.
